instruction:
You are given a Verilog module that uses hierarchical references and concatenation to set a value in a memory array. The memory is a 2-dimensional array called "memory" that is part of the top-level module "top". The value being set is a 2-bit value stored in the variable "temp". The code sets the value of the second element in the "memory" array to be a concatenation of "temp" and "temp" again. The code then displays the value of the second element in "memory" and checks if it was set correctly. If it was set correctly, the code displays a "PASS" message and exits. If it was not set correctly, the code displays an "ERROR" message and exits.

Your task is to write a Verilog module that performs the same operation as the code snippet provided. Your module should have a 2-dimensional array called "memory" that is the same size as the "memory" array in the top-level module "top". Your module should have a 2-bit input called "temp" that is used to set the value of the second element in "memory" to a concatenation of "temp" and "temp" again. Your module should also have a single output called "pass" that is set to 1 if the value of the second element in "memory" was set correctly and 0 otherwise.

Your module should be solvable within 200 lines of Verilog code.
